added_models.model: Human visual-evoked-potential LTP (EEG neuroplasticity) in schizophrenia patients

dose.quote: PF-03463275 increased long-term potentiation only in SZs with peak effects at 40 mg twice a day (∼75% GlyT1 occupancy) and with a profile suggestive of an inverted U dose response.
dose.note: PF-03463275 LTP peaked at 40 mg bid (~75% occupancy) with an inverted U; 60-80% occupancy was named the optimal window and set the trial doses.
dose.short: Human LTP peaked at 40 mg bid
dose.judgement: Dose-finding ran in patients themselves, so the dose model is human. Registered under NCT01911676 (first posted 2013-07-30), the same record as the later trial; the PET/LTP data are not posted there. Online 31 Jan 2018 sets the year; print Sep 2018.

dose.quote: PF-03463275 treatment, at doses demonstrated to engage the target, was safe and well-tolerated but did not produce a greater improvement in CIAS compared to CT alone.
dose.note: 40 and 60 mg bid, chosen from the LTP peak and highest occupancy, dosed with adherence checks; no MCCB gain over CT alone; programme ended.
dose.judgement: Reached, failed, abandoned: contra derived from efficacy, counted once. The trial paper sets its dose rationale beside the result ('Despite these controls, neither dose of the study drug improved MCCB scores'), so the comparison is stated. Registry results (2023-02-27) precede the epub (2 May 2023); year 2023 either way.

efficacy.quote: These findings provide support for a clinical trial to test the ability of PF-03463275 to enhance cognitive remediation toward addressing cognitive impairments associated with schizophrenia.
efficacy.note: Enhanced visual LTP in patients at 40 mg bid was read as neuroplasticity that would augment cognitive training in CIAS.
efficacy.short: Human LTP gain predicted CT augmentation
efficacy.judgement: The model's prediction is explicit: LTP enhancement should let PF-03463275 augment cognitive remediation. No patient comparison until the trial read out.

efficacy.quote: PF-03463275 in combination with CT was feasible, safe, and well-tolerated at the doses prescribed but did not produce greater improvement in CIAS compared to CT alone.

patient_trials.quote: Despite these controls, neither dose of the study drug improved MCCB scores in patients receiving CT.

efficacy.note: NCT01911676 (n=71 crossover, 5 weeks plus CT): neither 40 nor 60 mg bid improved the primary MCCB composite over CT alone.
efficacy.reason: Human LTP positive; MCCB trial flat
efficacy.judgement: A member's own human model with a prospective dose and efficacy test: it said 40 mg bid enhances neuroplasticity and should augment CT; the primary MCCB composite did not move at 40 or 60 mg. The source leaves the LTP-to-cognition link open ('further research is necessary to directly and conclusively link GLYT1 occupancy and/or LTP with the primary outcome'), hence unresolved. The trial's own day-7 LTP replication is 'to be reported elsewhere', so no engagement entry. Separate track from the rodent systems: different model and a different prediction (neuroplasticity augmenting CT, not symptom reversal).

added_models.model: Human ketamine-challenge working-memory fMRI in healthy volunteers

efficacy.quote: PF-03463275 did not attenuate any ketamine-induced effects but did improve working memory accuracy in healthy control subjects.
efficacy.note: At 10-40 mg bid PF-03463275 did not attenuate ketamine-induced working-memory circuit disruption, accuracy or symptom effects in healthy volunteers; the assay predicted no NMDA-R facilitation.
efficacy.judgement: Prediction of no effect on the assay's primary endpoint (ketamine-disrupted working-memory activation). A secondary, ketamine-independent accuracy gain at 40 mg is the one positive signal. The authors questioned the assay ('the current data question the utility of the reversal of ketamine effects as an assay') and proceeded on the LTP result. Registered under NCT01911676; data not posted there.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: presence of a pro-cognitive effect (none in the assay, none on the MCCB primary)
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by us: Surti 2023 lists the ketamine fMRI among its dose-selection inputs but does not set the null result beside the trial outcome. neg rests on the assay's own positive-call bar because the class has no successful drug to define class_threshold; same + direction_only is the alternative reading.
efficacy.quote: PF-03463275 in combination with CT was feasible, safe, and well-tolerated at the doses prescribed but did not produce greater improvement in CIAS compared to CT alone.

patient_trials.quote: Despite these controls, neither dose of the study drug improved MCCB scores in patients receiving CT.

efficacy.effect_size: 0: no attenuation of any ketamine-induced effect (working-memory activation, accuracy, reaction time, PANSS) at 10-40 mg bid in healthy volunteers
efficacy.class_threshold: attenuation of ketamine-induced working-memory disruption, the assay's positive call; no member drug has met it in humans, so the bar is the assay's own criterion rather than a successful member's effect size
efficacy.note: The assay flagged PF-03463275 as inactive on NMDA-R facilitation; the drug then gave no MCCB benefit over CT alone in NCT01911676.
efficacy.judgement: A model that predicted no effect for a drug that then failed: neg (matched, including a known failure), judged on what the data showed (decision 13). The ketamine-independent accuracy gain at 40 mg pointed the other way and is why the programme continued, but it is not the assay's primary readout. Org 25935's human ketamine challenge (D'Souza 2012) is the same system on a non-member and is not scored.

added_models.model: Rhesus monkey ketamine-induced spatial working-memory deficit

engagement.quote: In contrast, all doses of PF-3463275 alleviated the deficit in spatial working memory induced by ketamine.
engagement.note: PF-3463275 (0.01-0.17 mg/kg sc) reversed the ketamine-induced spatial working-memory deficit in rhesus at every dose, not the hallucinatory-like behaviours.
engagement.judgement: Member drug in the model (PF-3463275 is PF-03463275). First published use of the primate ketamine working-memory assay for the class; Neuroreport 31 Mar 2010.

engagement.quote: However, it contrasts with non-human primate (NHP) studies in which PF-03463275 and ORG-25935 reduced ketamine effects on working memory
engagement.note: In healthy volunteers PF-03463275 at 10-40 mg bid (44-76% occupancy) did not reverse ketamine-induced working-memory deficits; the source states the contrast with monkeys.
engagement.short: Human ketamine WM readout did not move
engagement.reason: Monkey reversal absent in dosed humans
engagement.judgement: The model's readout (reversal of ketamine-induced working-memory impairment) did not move in dosed humans at occupancies up to 76%; the source names the contrast and offers task over-training, infusion timing and species as reasons. A ketamine-independent accuracy gain at 40 mg is a different readout. Healthy volunteers count for engagement.

efficacy.quote: In contrast, all doses of PF-3463275 alleviated the deficit in spatial working memory induced by ketamine.
efficacy.note: Reversal of ketamine-induced working-memory deficits in rhesus was offered as translational support for GlyT1 inhibition as adjunctive treatment of cognitive dysfunction in schizophrenia.
efficacy.judgement: Prospective: eight years before the drug's human dose-finding and thirteen before its patient trial.

efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by us: Surti 2023 does not cite the primate study; the only stated primate-versus-human comparison is D'Souza 2018 in healthy volunteers (engagement cell).
efficacy.quote: PF-03463275 in combination with CT was feasible, safe, and well-tolerated at the doses prescribed but did not produce greater improvement in CIAS compared to CT alone.

patient_trials.quote: Despite these controls, neither dose of the study drug improved MCCB scores in patients receiving CT.

efficacy.note: PF-03463275 at 40 or 60 mg bid plus cognitive training gave no MCCB benefit over CT alone (NCT01911676, n=71).
efficacy.reason: Monkey WM reversal; patients no gain
efficacy.judgement: Different system from the rodent NMDA-antagonist tracks (primate, ketamine, delayed-response working memory, member drug dosed) and a prospective prediction from 2010, so its own track under this run's rule. Its human translation was already contradicted in 2018; the patient trial confirms.

considered_not_added: Roche media release, Basel 21 Jan 2014 (tier 5, FlashLyte/DayLyte 'failed to meet their primary endpoints'): a dating source for the existing bitopertin dose and efficacy contras, not a model system
Boehringer Ingelheim CONNEX topline release, Jan 2025 (tier 5): a dating source for the existing iclepertin 2025 entries, not a model system
Org 25935 human ketamine challenge (D'Souza 2012, 10.1038/npp.2011.295): Org 25935 is not a member drug; the same system is tracked only through PF-03463275 (D'Souza 2018)
Org 25935 rhesus PET-occupancy / ketamine cognition (Castner 2014, 10.1038/npp.2014.4): non-member drug

Spiros/Geerts 2014 QSP model of negative symptoms (10.3389/fphar.2014.00229, epub 2014-10-21, in_silico): published after both the bitopertin phase 2 inverted U and the Jan 2014 phase 3 misses; its output is a free-glycine concentration curve with no mapping to bitopertin dose or occupancy and no member-drug comparison stated beyond the introduction; not used to choose a dose. Would be a retrodiction without a quotable member comparison

Iclepertin PBPK drug-interaction model (CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2025, PMID 40556490) and exposure-haemoglobin PK/PD analysis (Front Pharmacol 2026, PMID 42499503): in-silico descriptors of DDI and Hb built on patient data; no class efficacy or dose-target prediction

Mouse TUNL working-memory / NMDA-antagonist network paper (Psychopharmacology 2026, PMID 42405981): a rodent NMDA-antagonist cognition system of the kind the draft already tracks (rodent-mk801-cognition-eeg), and post-CONNEX

Iclepertin patient EEG/MMN substudy (Surti 2023 cites 'improvements in cognition with BI 425809 were not correlated with MMN changes'): the engagement comparison for the existing rodent-mk801-cognition-eeg track, not a new system; not verified here
LTP track engagement cell: the trial's own day-7 VEP-LTP replication is 'to be reported elsewhere' (Surti 2023), so no engagement entry was written for human-vep-ltp-neuroplasticity
